newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Widspread ex-Amsterdam autumn cargo rates rises seen.
newsitem.headline: Widspread ex-Amsterdam autumn cargo rates rises seen.

text.p: More airlines in the Dutch market said they will be increasing or plan to increase ex-Netherland autumn air cargo rates.
Air Canada will be lifting its cargo rates by 5-12 percent on October 1 on all routes ex-Netherlands, Fred Veenendaal the director of the carrier's general sales agent, VIA, said.

In addition, British Airways World Cargo Dutch cargo manager, Matt Boon, said BA will probably increase rates from November 1 by around five to 10 percent, depending on the destination and also reflecting the weaker performance of the guilder against sterling.
From August 1, BA has already increased its cargo rate for vegetables by 10 Dutch cents a kilogram, representing a six to seven percent increase.

A Lufthansa Cargo spokesman in the Netherlands said the German airline would consider introducing a rates increase from October 1 but it had not yet been decided on the exact level of the rise yet. The high dollar was the main reason, he said.
And a Delta Airlines spokesman added the carrier is considering an increase in October of between five to 10 percent for general cargo ex-Netherlands.
Industry sources said national Dutch carrier, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines is also planning increases from late October but no confirmation was immeditaley available from the airline.

Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Air Hong Kong and Iberia Cargo have already said they plan a 10 percent increase from October 1 and September 1 respectively in ex-Europe rates.. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
